question: Which of the following production activities is the largest emitter of CO₂?
solution:
The correct answer is **Thermal power production**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Thermal power production** involves burning fossil fuels such as coal, oil, and natural gas, which release large amounts of CO2 into the atmosphere.
 
• **Coal-fired power plants** are the biggest contributors to CO2 emissions among all types of thermal power plants.
 
• The process of extracting, transporting, and burning fossil fuels in thermal power plants generates significant quantities of greenhouse gases.
 
• Reducing emissions from thermal power production is crucial for combating climate change and achieving international climate goals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Thermal Power Production** refers to the process of generating electricity by converting heat energy, typically from burning fossil fuels, into electrical energy. This method is widely used worldwide but is a major source of carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions, contributing significantly to global warming and air pollution.

 
 

 Fuel Type
 Description
 
 
 
 

 **Coal**
 Most widely used fuel in thermal power plants; highest CO2 emissions per unit of energy produced.
 
 

 **Natural Gas**
 Cleaner than coal; emits less CO2 but still a significant source of greenhouse gases.
 
 

 **Oil**
 Used in some thermal power plants; higher CO2 emissions than natural gas but lower than coal.
